However, the unredacted version has not been up-loaded, has not been assigned a number, and has not been admitted. And, of course, the Chamber needs in evidence the unredacted version. Has the unredacted version been up-loaded? It has been. I see Madam Registrar confirms that. Madam Registrar, that would be number --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, I would like you to assign a number -- a separate number to the unredacted version so that it can be admitted under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will become Exhibit D27, under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D27 is admitted under seal. As far as D6 is concerned, there was a translation issue. The Prosecution would verify and correct the translation. Has the revised translation been up-loaded?

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, just today, is my understanding, but it has been.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Under the same number -- 65 ter number?

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: My understanding is it was up-loaded under "D6."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D6. Madam Registrar, leave is granted to replace the new version of D6 in the e-court system. D9 is a document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Apart from replacing it, of course, the Chamber would still have to give a decision on admission. D6, in its new version, is admitted into evidence. I move to D9, which is a document under seal, but with the adequate caution we could deal with it in open session. An objection was raised against admission of D9. But, as I understand, the OTP has withdrawn its objection, but under the condition that the document would be admitted under seal. Is that correct, Mr. Groome?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour, we're quite a bit surprised by that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we could just have a moment. If there's another matter we could move on to, I'll try to call that document up and see if I can refresh my recollection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Transcript pages 2608 to 2611, and in private session 2619. It was Witness JF-007.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Mr. Hoffmann informs me that he believes that we've withdrawn this as an exhibit, but if I could have until -- I'm sorry, withdrawn its objection. Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: If I could just verify that and then come back to the Court the next time we're sitting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's our information as well, that the withdrawal was expressed on the 21st of January. Would there be any objection against admission under seal?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then D9 is admitted under seal. And if further verification would show that what you think to be the case and what we think you've done, that is, to withdraw the objection, then we still can reconsider that. D13, there was a missing first page to be up-loaded by the Stanisic Defence. Has this been done?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Apologies, it hasn't. But we can commit to making sure that it's done by Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we would revisit the matter on Monday --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Oh, I beg your pardon. I think what has to happen is we have to have it translated first. So if we can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It would first have to be translated, but, of course -- and then to be up-loaded. As a matter of fact, we instructed you to inform us when it was translated and up-loaded, but this was already a while ago. And since it was only one page, we expected the results.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: This is an oversight on our part and we do apologise, but we will make sure it's submitted for translation by Monday, at the latest.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So it's only one page. Could we -- by the end of next week, too?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hoffmann.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Just on Exhibit D13, if I remember correctly, Your Honours had some questions about this document to the Defence which weren't answered at the time. It was about whether this one, about a certain Slobodan Katanic, or another one would be correct. I don't know if those questions, in the Chamber's view, have been clarified or not, but I thought that was one of the issues why it was marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash saved us by the bell, because we now have an opportunity to further review pages 2914 to 17. Mr. Jordash will do the same, and then we'll have a look at whether we have received all the information we need for a final decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I can indicate now, Your Honours, that we haven't as yet investigated which date of birth is the correct one, and what we have done is simply relied upon a document. There are other documents relating to this particular gentleman. And we could, of course, set out and investigate when his date of birth was, or the Prosecution could simply indicate whether they actually dispute the existence of this man and the detail in the exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perfectly a matter for further conversations and perhaps to see what the Prosecution still expects from the Stanisic, or the other way around.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours, we didn't object at the time, and we didn't have any questions. At the moment, I also have no verification of the date of birth, but we had no issue with the admission of this document. I was just noting your questions to the Defence at the time about the Defence position on whether the one or the other document is true.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. So, therefore, as far as admission is concerned, there seems to be no problem. Then we are still waiting for the translation and for uploading of the document, and we'll hear from you by the end of next week, Mr. Jordash. Then I move to D14, which is a document under seal. Yes. There has been an issue as to what to do with the document, which contains, as it was emphasised by the Prosecution, a negative answer to a question whether the MUP records and archives show that a certain person - I think we're talking about Witness JF-005 - worked for the special forces, yes or no. The Chamber admits D14, under seal, but the Chamber would be assisted in properly attaching weight to this document if the parties would present further submissions on the fact whether or not this person worked in that position, and to present any further evidence to that. Therefore, we admit the document in evidence, but we give a clear signal to the parties that in order to be better capable of giving weight to this document, that we would like to hear further submissions on this and similar matters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm informed that apart from this matter, that finally the document can only be admitted if an English translation is attached and up-loaded. So, therefore, the Chamber -- well, I've just said it's not a final decision of the Chamber. We'd like to have the English translation first. But what is to be found in the document needs -- the Chamber needs further assistance in exactly weighing this evidence, and invites the parties to make further submissions on this matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, as you'll recall, the concern that I raised was Serbia's repeated representations that their archives have been -- so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You said -- you explained to us that these situations happened before, that you got similar information which then later turned out to be wrong. Now, of course, the Chamber -- that's what you said. If there's any documentary evidence showing that, We asked this for a different person, we got this answer at that moment, and it turned out to be true because they wrote us at a later stage that -- or we received evidence. So that's exactly the kind of information the Chamber would like to receive, because on face value, it seems to be denial, although saying that we find anything in the records can mean two things; that it didn't happen, or that it wasn't recorded. I mean, there are several options. Now in order to better able to understand the probative value of this document, the Chamber would like to hear from the Prosecution of similar experiences, well documented, so that the Chamber is better able to assess what weight to give to this document, phrased in the way as it is, because you specifically have drawn our attention to the way in which the denial or the negative finding was phrased.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, and it may require that the Prosecution call a representative of Serbia to explain their position with respect to these. But I will look into the matter and decide what's the best course to take.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, of course. Nothing opposes, apart perhaps from the time granted to you in your 65 ter list, to receive evidence, even witness testimony, in respect of this. Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honour, could I just seek some clarification? What the Chamber is looking for is submissions on the -- I suppose the meaning of documents which emanate from this source?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Not only from this source. Perhaps also from the source. I do not know. I mean, the Chamber is not fully acquainted with all the -- if it is source, then we would like to hear that from the Prosecution that documents coming from this source have turned out to be inaccurate several times; or information from whatever source about members of Unit A, B, or C, have turned out to be inaccurate several times. The Chamber is just not aware, and that's the reason why we admit this document into evidence, but in order to better assess the probative value the Chamber would like to have substantiation of the matters that were raised by the Prosecution or any other matter which may shed some light. And if, at a later stage, you would call witnesses on this matter, then you could say, This and this is our experience, but apart from that we intend to call Witness A, B, or C, to shed further light on this or similar documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: But Your Honours are not looking -- I just want to be certain about this aspect. Your Honours are not looking for substantive submissions on the witness and whether -- our respective positions on whether the witness was a member of a particular unit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At this moment, we are seeking additional information which allows us to better understand the probative value. If there would be clear evidence -- if you would say -- or you would say, I have five pictures and four telephone conversations which clearly showed that he was a member, then, of course, that could shed some light as well. But at this moment, the Chamber is primarily focusing on a further substantiation of the matters raised in relation to this document by the Prosecution. But we do not exclude, because the document is just saying, We don't have records of this person being in this service, yes or no. I can imagine that, at a later stage, the parties -- you to say, This is correct, or you to say, This is not correct, that would further focus on the substance, not any more directly related to the probative value or the weight to be given to this specific document, which is just one element in what apparently is the substance of the problem, was he or was he not.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then I know it's getting later and later. I have one final matter on my agenda, which relates to D19. D19, there was an objection. The Prosecution requested an opportunity to further verify the origin of the document. And then on the 9th of February, the Prosecution made a submission in which it states that it verified the origin of the exhibit and informs the Trial Chamber and the Defence that, according to records in the possession of the Office of the Prosecutor, the Witness Slobodan Lazarevic, provided the document on the 4th of January, and therefore does not object any further to the authenticity of D19. Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Therefore, since there were no other objections, as I understand, it's ready to be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D19 is admitted into evidence. I am through my list, and I don't think that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I've gone through my MFI list. First question: Any other matters as far as MFI's are concerned?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, there were two other MFIs with respect to the Witness Slobodan Lazarevic. I refer Your Honours to transcript of 9 of February, transcript pages 3487 and 3489. If you recall, this was the -- the two documents that purported to be an indictment and an arrest warrant. It was very late in the day, and I simply noted my objection. And without having time to express it, the documents were marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that D25 and D26?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I'm sorry, D25 and D26.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D25 and D26. I think -- let me just check.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The Chamber will deal with this matter, and invites the parties to wait until they've heard from the Chamber, and then only to decide on any follow-up of D25 and D26.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Will the Prosecution have an opportunity to put its position with respect to the admissibility? I'm not sure what Your Honour is referring to, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. No. Further the Chamber will address the matter, and of course we'll also at that moment -- it's not just about admissibility - that's the issue - but that is related to it, and therefore the parties are invited to wait to make any further submissions until the Chamber has addressed the matter first, and then you'll be given an opportunity.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Mr. Hoffmann has two matters regarding MFIs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Hoffmann.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Very briefly, I wanted to note that for Exhibit P260, the document that we talked about a while ago, we have already up-loaded and released the one, which is the underlying document for Exhibit P107. You already assigned the numbers, pending the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you remind me what number Madam Registrar had a assigned to it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P260. And there was no need to have it admitted under seal, was it?

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, let me just -- yes, that was the underlying document, giving further details so that the Chamber could consider P107 and P260 in context. P260 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. The other issue is just a matter of the status of another exhibit. It's Exhibit P166. It's currently under seal. utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'll consider it, we'll have a look at it. Of course, I was not prepared to deal with that. Could the Defence teams also look into the matter. We'd like to hear from you by next -- no, let's not say if you do not make any -- we'd like to hear from you, an answer, whether you would or would not object to making P166 a public document by Wednesday, and the Chamber would then decide. Any other matter, Mr. Hoffmann?

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Yes, one final matter. I don't know if and when the Chamber wanted to deal with the exhibits and prior statements of Witness Kovacevic. utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we will consider that, and I'm not going to immediately rule on your request. We'll further consider the matter and let you know most likely in the middle of next week. utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Groome. Mr. Jordash, no further issues?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, the same. Then we adjourn, and we'll resume Monday --

utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.
